findings.issue_text: Global login predicate excludes private organization-linked IdPs unless BROKER_PUBLIC=true, incorrectly making them unavailable for ORG_ONLY/ALL queries even after their organization is identified

OrganizationCacheTest registers cleanup using the literal alias "alias" instead of the created aliases (idp-alias-* and idp-alias-20), leaking IdPs and risking cleanup failures or cross-test contamination

goldens.comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Global login predicate excludes private organization-linked IdPs unless BROKER_PUBLIC=true, incorrectly making them unavailable for ORG_ONLY/ALL queries even after their organization is identified

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at the diff, the getLoginPredicate() adds a filter that allows IDPs where either (1) organizationId is null, OR (2) BROKER_PUBLIC is true. This is a basic filter for what qualifies as a 'login IDP'. The actual getForLogin() method in the delegate (JpaIdentityProviderStorageProvider, not shown but referenced) handles the FetchMode logic separately - ORG_ONLY and ALL modes would query organization-linked IDPs differently. The predicate is just determining if an IDP is 'available for login' in general, not filtering the final results. The test in the diff shows ORG_ONLY correctly returns 5 org-linked IDPs, confirming the behavior works as expected.
